h1: The Resume Statistics Everyone Cites That Are Already Out of Date

persona.name: HR / Talent-Management Leader
persona.lens: A people-strategy leader who cites hiring/workforce stats in reports and decks and needs them dated correctly and current, including the AI-resume-fraud figures competitors omit, so their own claims hold up under scrutiny.
persona.why: This is a myth-busting, stat-accuracy piece (dating stats to survey year, surfacing an omitted data point) — squarely the 'myth-busting industry articles' and 'named research' register this persona reads and cites, not an operational screening how-to.

gaps_to_own: Per-stat survey-year dating: all three publish under a single page-level year badge ("2025", "2023") while blending stats from different years underneath — none anchors each individual stat to its original survey year, which is this asset's core angle.

AI-fabricated/exaggerated resume figures: resume.io and standout-cv carry no AI section at all; testgorilla's "Statistics about resumes and AI" covers AI writing-tool adoption, not fabrication or lying rates — the specific figures this asset adds are absent industry-wide.
ATS filter accuracy/usage stats appear on only one of three winners (standout-cv) — thin coverage elsewhere, worth a stronger own if it fits the angle.

ai_overview: entirely off-topic homonym collision — it defines "CV" as the statistical **coefficient of variation** (σ/μ, with population/sample formulas, percentage form, consistency check, limitations), not curriculum vitae. No resume/CV-career content at all.
